body:
# Independent audit: genuine criticality and nearest-neighbor residual roots


`candidate 23a10e01167cf706`.
Result: **PASS** for the stated n=1, d>=2 theorem and its separately
scoped quantitative reserve.

## 1. Measures, containing caps, and the exact step comparison

The assumption of a positive-volume source fiber implies that the
mixed measure is the relevant H_d measure and that its total mass is
positive. Boundedness leaves finitely many integer fibers. The source
is an actual mixed point and a global maximizer by hypothesis; the
lemma does not purport to construct such a point.

The source captured fraction at most 1/2 forces a nonzero continuous
normal and a positive-volume strict source residual. If the strict
residual at base -1 is empty, convexity of `C intersect H^c` proves
that no strict residual point can occur at any integer base below
zero: its segment to a source residual point would meet the fiber
at -1 in the strict residual. This is a statement about actual sets,
including absent and boundary-only fibers, not an inference from a
zero volume.

For the finite tilt `a -> a-L`, every negative trace grows into a
fiber already captured in full, the source trace stays fixed, and
every positive trace decreases. Finitely many compact fibers allow
one finite L that strictly excludes every positive-base fiber.
Every tilted closed cap still contains the same point of depth Q,
so its mass is at least Q. Monotonicity gives the reverse inequality.
Consequently the original critical cap already has zero captured
d-volume at every positive base. The exact mass identity

    Q=sum_(j<0) |C_j| + p |C_0|

is justified. It does not assert that all original positive-base cap
traces are empty as sets. Tangent traces may remain and carry zero
d-volume. All original closed halfspaces, including any full boundary
fiber of a purely integer alternative, are handled in the comparisons.

## 2. Prefix root estimates use only nonempty BM summands

For a nonempty fiber at -k and a positive-volume fiber at 1,

    (C_-k+k C_1)/(k+1) subset C_0

is an actual convex combination. Ordinary BM yields, after normalizing
`|C_0|^(1/d)=1`,

    |C_-k|^(1/d)<=1-k(b-1),  b=|C_1|^(1/d).

A negative right side excludes existence of that fiber; a zero right
side permits a nonempty lower-dimensional fiber and assigns it zero
mass. An absent fiber contributes no mass and is never used as a BM
summand. Thus the positive-part prefix sum is valid. When b=0, the
claimed strict residual inequality and quantitative reserve follow
directly, without invoking this prefix estimate with an empty set.

At the centroid of any positive neighboring fiber, every nonvertical
ambient containing cap captures at least the ordinary Grünbaum
fraction of that own fiber. A purely integer containing cap includes
the whole fiber. These are actual mixed points, so global maximality
gives `Q>=gamma |C_j|`. This is exactly where global, rather than
merely local, maximality is used.

## 3. Exact constants and strictness

The binomial estimates prove `1/3<gamma<=4/9` in every integer d>=2.
They give the claimed residual-root bound

    (1-gamma)^(1/d)>=sqrt(5)/3>5/7.

For d=2, a failure of the nearest-neighbor estimate would require
`b>sqrt(2)` under p<=1/2. The prefix bound allows only k=1,2 and gives

    Q<=1/2+(2-sqrt(2))^2+(3-2sqrt(2))^2
      =47/2-16sqrt(2)<8/9.

The last comparison is equivalent to `sqrt(2)>407/288`; squaring
positive quantities gives `165888>165649`. This contradicts
`Q>=(4/9)b^2>8/9`. The same calculation with `b>=sqrt(2)` rules out
equality as well.

For d>=3, a failure would force `b>2^(1-1/d)>3/2`. Only the first
left fiber could then have positive volume, of size less than 1/8.
The upper mass bound 5/8 contradicts
`Q>2^(d-1)/3>=4/3`. For strictness independently of a presumed
failure, b>=3/2 gives the same upper bound 5/8 and a lower bound
strictly larger than 9/8. Thus b<3/2, while
`f_0>=2^(-1/d)>3/4`. The strict nearest-neighbor inequality follows.

Under the additional p<=gamma assumption, b>=10/7 allows only the
first two left masses and bounds their sum by
`(4/7)^d+(1/7)^d<=17/49`. The exact step identity and neighboring
centroid lower bound would give

    100 gamma/49 <= Q <= gamma+17/49,

or `51 gamma<=17`, contradicting gamma>1/3. Hence b<10/7.
Subtracting half the neighboring residual root from the source root
gives exactly the strict reserve

    (sqrt(5)/3-5/7)|C_0|^(1/d).

This reserve uses both an empty strict neighboring residual and the
stronger own-fraction bound p<=gamma. It is not established for every
case of the main inequality, and the corrected statement respects
that distinction.

## 4. Nonempty strict residuals and limits

If both neighboring strict residuals are nonempty, each contains a
point with a strictly positive margin from the cap boundary. One
common sufficiently small epsilon therefore makes both compact
stricter cuts nonempty, even if one has zero d-volume. Their
Minkowski midpoint is in the source strict residual. BM gives the
desired root inequality for those compact cuts. As epsilon decreases
to zero they increase to the original strict residuals. Continuity
from below of finite Lebesgue measure proves the stated limit.
No selected points need converge, no maximization is interchanged
with a limit, and no empty set is used in BM.

This also separates the important tangent case: a neighboring closed
residual may be a facet while its strict residual is empty. Such a
neighbor belongs to the step-comparison case, not the compact
approximation case.

## 5. Scope

The proof controls every actual ambient critical cap satisfying its
own-fiber fraction assumption, including oblique caps. It does not
assume a fiber centroid for the selected global point, a no-heavy
condition, positive volume in every neighboring fiber, or a finite
three-fiber body. It does not establish the hypothesis for every
critical cap or justify a terminal KKT stopping argument.

One small expository distinction was relayed to root: when describing
failure of the MAIN hypothesis at other states of a chain, the own
fraction threshold is 1/2; gamma is the threshold for the additional
uniform reserve. This does not affect any proved statement.

Finally the step comparison uses ordering of the entire integer base
by one coordinate. It does not extend from an empty neighboring fiber
on a primitive line in Z^n, n>=2, to the off-line fibers. A separate
complete-base counterexample is recorded in
`candidate ba5090fdb5cfb1e1`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
